Great tasting water and save a LOT of money - I’ve been buying these filters for years and I love them. They cost a fraction of the name brand ones sold at the big box appliance store that are meant to go in my Samsung refrigerator. They give me good tasting, clean water that we use for drinking and cooking. I can even guess at how much money I’ve saved over the 10 years I’ve owned this refrigerator but I know it significant. We change the filters about 4 times per year. Would probably need to change more often if we didn’t also buy a lot of bottled water just for convenience. Water flow is reduced as filter fills with contaminants so I know it is catching the bad stuff I don’t want to drink. We also drink a lot of coffee in my house and use the filtered water from refrigerator to make it. I get noticeably better tasting coffee useing the water from these filters that’s I do using tap water. Would recommend these to anyone wanting good tasting water without being ripped off by the expensive filters.

I got these wrap filters after the disc filters failed miserably with my Presto 2-12 cup machine.

- These filters don't look as neatly buttoned up as shown on the label. They are all paper.
- These filters work much better than those useless disc-types.
- They don't take all the flavor out of coffee.
- I think they work best for me if I dampen the top before I start the percolator.
- The center hole is easy to find but the side holes are almost invisible.

Tip: After getting the center hole onto the basket's "pipe", add a little of the coffee before pushing the filter down. This helps me when I am trying to fold in the sides.

I almost wish these were made to just fit around the sides & to the top of the basket. Folding over is awkward & depending on how you do it, some grinds spill out anyway.

Personally, I am going to look for a re-usable filter that just sits inside my basket. I only need a filter when I am using finer grinds.

Saved My GE Refrigerator - Official Part!!! - I own a GE Profile refrigerator. It came with the house I bought and I never had to deal with moving it. So to get it to fit, I had to take the doors off. Everything came off pretty quickly and easily. The problem though, was the part I'm reviewing. FYI, it's officially called a union connector. Upon removal of the connector, it bent/destroyed the metal "teeth" that keeps the water line in place. When time came to reassemble the door, the house kept falling out because the metal "teeth" didn't grip the water line to keep it flush against the rubber O-ring in the connector. Thus I had slow drip water leaks.

I went to Lowe's thinking they had the part and they did, but it was a 3rd party connector. While I don't doubt that it works, it didn't work on my refrigerator. The leaks persisted and thus, I came to Amazon to see if they had the part... and they did!

Since having purchased the item on Amazon, it works beautifully. It came in a GE bag, looks identical to the one I broke, and MOST IMPORTANTLY STOPPED MY LEAK!!
